newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Polynesian airlines to buy Boeing 737-300.
newsitem.headline: Polynesian airlines to buy Boeing 737-300.

text.p: Polynesian Airlines on Friday signalled its return to financial health by the announcement that it is to buy a Boeing 737-300 aircraft, chairman of Polynesian and Western Samoan Aviation Minister, Tuilaepa Sa'ilele Malielegaoi, said.
The aircraft is currently leased on an offbalance sheet operating basis from International Lease Finance Corp and it will be converted to a conditional sale agreement on December 30, Polynesian said.
"This is a significant event for the country and the airline following the company's recovery from the difficult days of the past," Malielegaoi said.
The company reported heavy losses in 1993 and 1994 before a restructuring.
Malielegaoi said the sale agreement would have a positive impact on the company's present and future cashflows and profitability.
